mainTopic: Separating a חתן and כלה during wedding-time אבילות compared with נדה, and the ban on first relations on Friday night and מוצאי שבת
overview: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's 'likewise' about a נדה applies only before the first relations, while a mourning חתן sleeps apart from his wife even after them. That seems to treat אבילות as a prohibition people take more lightly than נדה. But a wife in אבילות may pour her husband's cup, make his bed and wash him, which a נדה may not do. The first answer is that sleeping apart applies to the husband's אבילות, while serving him is allowed in the wife's אבילות. The גמרא defends this distinction against several challenges from the wording of two ברייתות ('father of the groom or mother of the bride', 'likewise', 'with him'). רב אשי gives a different answer: wedding-time אבילות is special. The רבנן already eased it by letting the seven wedding days come before the seven mourning days, so people might take it lightly and extra separation is needed. Finally the גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule against first relations on Friday night or מוצאי שבת. It asks why מוצאי שבת is included, and רבי זירא's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: How to read the ברייתא's 'and likewise' about a נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's 'and likewise' refers to a חתן whose wife became a נדה before he had relations with her. In that case he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: and likewise, if his wife became a נדה before he had relations with her, he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining how to read the ברייתא's words 'וכן' (and likewise) correctly. The separation applies to a נדה only before the first relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a mourner, the couple sleeps apart even after their first relations. With a נדה, the separation rule applies only if they have not yet been together. So the 'likewise' compares the two cases only in that narrower situation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (introduces a reading of an earlier text)
She became a נדה (began to menstruate)
Sleeps among the men, so he is never alone with her

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
And likewise, one whose wife became a menstruating woman
and he had not yet had relations with her —
he sleeps among the men,
and his wife sleeps among the women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-reads the ברייתא discussed just before this section.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'likewise' about a נדה applies only before the first relations, while a mourner sleeps apart even after them.

steps.title: Does this mean אבילות is lighter than נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא: mourners must sleep apart even after their first relations, but a נדה only before. That suggests people treat אבילות more lightly, so more separation is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that, in his view, mourning is a more lenient prohibition than נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out an idea hidden in the ברייתא. It is setting up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a 'lenient' prohibition means one people take lightly and might break. That is why mourners need extra separation. With נדה, the prohibition is severe enough that after the first relations the couple can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a conclusion drawn from a text, often to be questioned)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lighter' here does not mean we worry less. It means the prohibition is taken less seriously, so we actually worry more and add more separation.

phrases.english: Is that to say that mourning
is more lenient in his view than a menstruating woman?
phrases.notes: 'Lenient' here means a rule people treat lightly, so they need more fences to keep it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the reading given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא implies that אבילות is treated as a lighter prohibition than נדה.

steps.title: The rules of serving a husband suggest the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a נדה may not pour her husband's cup, make his bed or wash him. A ברייתא says a woman in אבילות may do all three. So the rabbis seem to worry less about אבילות than about נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יצחק בר חנינא said in the name of רב הונא: a נדה does every task a wife does for her husband except pouring his cup, making his bed and washing his face, hands and feet. Yet about mourning a ברייתא teaches: although he may not force his wife to put on eye makeup or rouge, she may pour his cup, make his bed and wash his face, hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 2 by pointing to rules that seem to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the cup, making the bed and washing are close, intimate acts. They are banned for a נדה but allowed during אבילות, so the rabbis seem less worried about relations during mourning. Yet the ברייתא made mourners sleep apart even after their first relations, so the two sources point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Pouring (mixing) his drink into the cup
In truth they said (introduces a firm rule)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chanina say
that Rav Huna said:
All tasks that a woman does for her husband —
a menstruating woman does for her husband,
except for pouring the cup
and making the bed,
and washing his face, hands, and feet.
Whereas regarding mourning it was taught:
Although they said

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לָכוֹף אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ
phrases.english: a man is not permitted to force his wife
to paint her eyes or to rouge her face,
in truth they said:
she pours the cup for him,
and makes the bed for him,
and washes his face, hands, and feet for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that אבילות needs more separation than נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Intimate acts are banned for a נדה but allowed during אבילות, which shows less worry about אבילות. That clashes with the stricter sleeping rule for mourners.

steps.title: His mourning versus her mourning
steps.stepSummary: The sleeping-apart rule is about the husband's אבילות. The permission for her to serve him is about the wife's אבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is about his mourning; there it is about her mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by showing that the two sources are talking about different people in mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband is the mourner, the ברייתא makes them sleep apart, because he might not hold back. When the wife is the mourner, she would not go along with it, so she may still serve him with these intimate acts. So the idea that אבילות is taken more lightly than נדה stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)

steps.whatToRemember: A husband in אבילות must sleep apart from his wife. When the wife is in אבילות, she may still pour his cup, make his bed and wash him, even though a נדה may not.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here — in his mourning,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the sleeping-apart rule for the mourning חתן.

phrases.english: there — in her mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בַּאֲבֵילוּת דִּידֵיהּ, כָּאן בַּאֲבֵילוּת דִּידַהּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same mourning situation, so they appeared to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Separation applies when the husband mourns; the serving acts are allowed when the wife mourns.

steps.title: The ברייתא mentions both his parent and her parent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists both the father of the חתן and the mother of the כלה, so it seems to make no distinction between his אבילות and hers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'the father of the groom or the mother of the bride'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 4. The ברייתא that requires sleeping apart mentions a death on her side too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said sleeping apart applies only when the husband is the mourner. But the ברייתא includes the case where the כלה's mother died, which is the wife's אבילות. So it looks like sleeping apart applies to her אבילות as well.

phrases.english: But it teaches: the father of the groom
or the mother of the bride!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָבִיו שֶׁל חָתָן אוֹ אִמָּהּ שֶׁל כַּלָּה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the distinction made in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 4's claim that sleeping apart applies only to the husband's אבילות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the bride's mother too, which suggests sleeping apart also applies when the wife is the mourner.

steps.title: Both parents are mentioned for the other mourning rules
steps.stepSummary: Mentioning both sides refers to the rest of the ברייתא's rules, not to sleeping apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches both, that is about the rest of the rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'father of the groom or mother of the bride' wording covers the other rules in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has several rules, such as finishing the wedding and then keeping אבילות. Those apply no matter whose parent died. Sleeping apart is limited to the husband's אבילות.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it is about the rest.
phrases.notes: He means the other rules in that ברייתא, not the rule about sleeping apart.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Listing both parents means every rule, including sleeping apart, applies to both
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parents are listed for the other rules; sleeping apart applies only to his אבילות

steps.title: A ברייתא treats his אבילות and hers alike
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes a husband mourning his in-law and a wife mourning her in-law with the same rules, and says nothing about sleeping apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really a difference between his אבילות and hers? A ברייתא teaches: if a man's father-in-law or mother-in-law died, he cannot make his wife use eye paint or rouge. Instead he turns over his bed and keeps אבילות with her. Likewise, if her father-in-law or mother-in-law died, she may not use eye paint or rouge. Instead she turns over her bed and keeps אבילות with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that seems to give the husband's אבילות and the wife's אבילות identical rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case of this ברייתא (her in-laws died), the husband is the real mourner. Yet the ברייתא lists the same rules as in her case and does not require sleeping apart. It even says she keeps אבילות 'with him', which suggests they stay together.

keyTerms.meaning: Painting the eyes with כחל (eye makeup)
Turns over his bed, an old mourning practice

steps.confusionAlert: Read the in-law words carefully. In the first case his in-law died, which is her parent, so it is her אבילות. In the second case her in-law died, which is his parent, so it is his אבילות.

phrases.english: And is there a difference between his mourning
and her mourning?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: מִי שֶׁמֵּת חָמִיו אוֹ חֲמוֹתוֹ —
phrases.english: But it was taught: one whose father-in-law or mother-in-law died
phrases.notes: His in-laws are her parents, so this first case is really her אבילות.

phrases.english: cannot force his wife
to paint her eyes or to rouge her face,
rather he turns over his bed,
and keeps mourning with her.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הִיא שֶׁמֵּת חָמִיהָ אוֹ חֲמוֹתָהּ —
phrases.english: And likewise she, whose father-in-law or mother-in-law died
phrases.notes: Her in-laws are his parents, so this case is really his אבילות.

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ רַשָּׁאָה לִהְיוֹת כּוֹחֶלֶת וְלִהְיוֹת פּוֹקֶסֶת,
phrases.english: is not allowed to paint her eyes or to rouge her face,
rather she turns over her bed
and keeps mourning with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שָׁאנֵי בֵּין אֲבֵילוּת דִּידֵיהּ לַאֲבֵילוּת דִּידַהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the distinction from steps 4 and 6, using a different ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between his אבילות and hers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא gives both cases the same rules and does not require separation when he is the mourner.

steps.title: Add sleeping apart to the husband's case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא should be read so that, in his אבילות, he sleeps among the men and she sleeps among the women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach this about his mourning: he sleeps among the men and his wife sleeps among the women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how the ברייתא is read. The case of his אבילות should include the sleeping-apart rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving up the distinction, the גמרא says the ברייתא's second case (his אבילות) really includes separation. This keeps the ברייתא in line with the rule from the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it (read the ברייתא) this way

phrases.english: Teach regarding his mourning:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is telling us to add these words to the second case of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: he sleeps among the men
and his wife sleeps among the women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by changing the reading of the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא with added words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives both cases the same rules, with no separation
steps.terutzMaskana: In his אבילות, the ברייתא should be read as requiring them to sleep apart

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'likewise'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'וכן' suggests the two cases have the same rules.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 8. The ברייתא links the second case to the first with the word 'likewise'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his case had an extra rule of sleeping apart, the ברייתא would not call it 'likewise'. The word suggests the two cases are fully the same.

phrases.english: But it teaches "and likewise"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new reading from step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: Adding the sleeping-apart rule only to his case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Likewise' suggests both cases have the same rules.

steps.title: 'Likewise' is only about makeup
steps.stepSummary: 'Likewise' means only that the eye-paint and rouge rule is the same in both cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'likewise', it means about eye paint and rouge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'likewise' compares only one detail, the ban on makeup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Likewise' does not mean every rule is the same. It refers to the makeup rule, so his case can still have the extra rule of sleeping apart.

phrases.english: When it teaches this, it is about eye paint and rouge.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Likewise' makes both cases the same in every rule
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Likewise' refers only to the makeup ban

steps.title: But she keeps אבילות 'with him'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says she keeps אבילות 'with him', which sounds like sharing a bed, the opposite of sleeping apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'with him'. Doesn't that mean with him in bed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again from another word in the ברייתא, 'עמו', 'with him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his אבילות the ברייתא says she keeps אבילות 'with him'. If that means in the same bed, it directly contradicts the claim that they must sleep apart.

phrases.english: But it teaches "with him",
doesn't that mean with him in bed?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עִמּוֹ קָתָנֵי, מַאי לָאו עִמּוֹ בַּמִּטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge to the step 8 reading, from the word 'with him'
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in his אבילות they sleep apart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'With him' seems to mean together in bed, so they do not sleep apart.

steps.title: 'With him' means at home, in his presence
steps.stepSummary: 'With him' means in the house, in front of him, as רב told his son חייא to keep אבילות in front of his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means with him in the house. As רב told his son חייא: in front of her, keep אבילות; not in front of her, you don't need to keep אבילות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'with him' means she shows אבילות in his presence at home, not that she shares his bed. It backs this up with רב's instruction to his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mourning 'with' your spouse for an in-law means showing mourning in front of them, out of respect. רב's advice to חייא shows this idea: the in-law mourning is kept for the spouse's sake, in their presence. So 'with him' says nothing about the bed, and the sleeping-apart rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of her; in her presence

steps.whatToRemember: The distinction holds: when the husband is the mourner, the couple sleep apart. The other rules, like the makeup ban and showing mourning at home, are the same for both of them.

phrases.english: No, with him in the house.
And as רב said to חייא his son:
in front of her, keep mourning;
not in front of her, do not keep mourning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and closes this line of challenges
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets a word, with support from a story about רב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With him' means in the same bed
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With him' means in his presence at home; separation in his אבילות still applies

steps.title: רב אשי: wedding-time mourning is easy to take lightly
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the original contradiction another way. Ordinary אבילות is serious, so nobody takes it lightly. Wedding-time אבילות was made lenient by the רבנן, so people might disregard it, and extra separation is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Can you compare the mourning here to mourning in general? Mourning in general is strict, and people won't come to treat it lightly. The mourning here, since the רבנן were lenient about it, people will come to treat it lightly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer to the question from steps 2 and 3, without needing the his-versus-her distinction. He says the wedding case is a special kind of אבילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why a mourner must sleep apart when in general the רבנן seem less worried about אבילות than about נדה. רב אשי says ordinary אבילות is taken seriously, so a wife may serve her husband without worry. At a wedding the רבנן already eased things, letting the wedding go ahead first, so people may take this אבילות lightly. That is why more separation is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. Step 4 says it depends on whose אבילות it is. רב אשי says wedding-time אבילות is unusual: because the רבנן eased it, people may disregard it, so they made the separation stricter.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common idea in רבנן's rules: when a law has been made lenient, people may stop respecting it, so a protective rule is added.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Are you comparing the mourning here
to mourning in general?
Mourning in general is strict,
and people won't come to treat it lightly.
The mourning here,
since the רבנן were lenient about it,
people will come to treat it lightly.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מִי קָמְדַמֵּית אֲבִילוּתָא דְהָכָא לַאֲבִילוּתָא דְעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from step 4's to the contradiction in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes wedding-time אבילות from ordinary אבילות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All אבילות is the same, so being lenient about her serving him should mean being lenient about sleeping together
steps.terutzMaskana: Wedding-time אבילות was eased by the רבנן and may be taken lightly, so stricter separation is needed

steps.title: Which leniency did the רבנן give?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what leniency רב אשי meant, and suggests it is the permission to perform בעילת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the leniency? If you say it is what the ברייתא teaches, that he performs the בעילת מצוה and then separates from her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב אשי meant by "the רבנן were lenient" in wedding-time אבילות. It offers a first guess, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's answer depends on there really being a leniency in this case. So the גמרא looks for one in the ברייתא. The first candidate is that the groom may perform the בעילת מצוה even though a parent has died.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a guess the גמרא is about to test)
The first relations of the marriage, done as a מצוה

phrases.english: What is the leniency?
If you say it is that which it teaches:
He performs the מצוה intercourse and separates —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is behind רב אשי's claim of a leniency
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was the leniency the רבנן gave in wedding-time אבילות?

steps.title: That is not a leniency, since mourning has not started
steps.stepSummary: Allowing the בעילת מצוה is no leniency at all, because אבילות does not take hold until the body leaves the house (רבי אליעזר) or the גולל is closed (רבי יהושע).
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because אבילות has not yet come upon him: according to רבי אליעזר, not until the body goes out of the doorway of the house; according to רבי יהושע, not until the grave-cover is sealed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first guess. Permitting the בעילת מצוה is not a special softening of אבילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעילת מצוה happens while the body is still in the house, before burial. At that point the groom is not yet an אבל at all, according to both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. So nothing about אבילות was relaxed.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא חָל עָלָיו אֲבִילוּתָא,
phrases.english: There it is because mourning has not taken effect on him,
whether according to Rabbi Eliezer,
not until it goes out of the doorway of the house,
phrases.notes: "It" means the body being carried out for burial.

phrases.english: or according to Rabbi Yehoshua,
not until the grave-cover is sealed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא חָל עָלָיו אֲבִילוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the guess offered in step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the suggestion that the בעילת מצוה is the leniency
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: At the time of the בעילת מצוה, אבילות has not yet begun under either opinion, so permitting it relaxes nothing

steps.title: The leniency is wedding week first, mourning after
steps.stepSummary: The real leniency is that the groom keeps שבעת ימי המשתה first and only then the seven days of אבילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is what the ברייתא teaches: he keeps the seven days of the feast, and afterward he keeps the seven days of אבילות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true leniency. The groom pushes off his mourning to celebrate the wedding week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the groom is already an אבל, yet the רבנן let him delay אבילות for seven days. That is a real softening. This is why רב אשי worried that people might take wedding-time אבילות lightly and therefore required extra separation.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven days of wedding celebration

steps.whatToRemember: The leniency is that mourning is pushed off until after the wedding week. Because of that leniency, the couple must stay apart so the groom does not treat his אבילות lightly.

phrases.english: Rather, it is that which it teaches:
He observes the seven days of the feast,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹהֵג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי אֲבֵילוּת.
phrases.english: and afterward he observes the seven days of mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָתָנֵי: נוֹהֵג שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמִּשְׁתֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected guess with the correct leniency
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leniency is that the groom delays the seven days of אבילות until after the seven days of the wedding feast

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: no first relations Friday night or Saturday night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line of the ברייתא: the groom may not have first relations with a virgin bride on Friday night or on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: In either case he may not have relations, not on Friday night and not on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the ברייתא. This is a setup for a question it will ask next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line names two times when the first relations are forbidden: the night that begins שבת and the night that ends it. The גמרא will next ask why each one is included.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said", a way of quoting an earlier source in order to discuss it
Here, the night that begins שבת (Friday night)
The night after שבת ends (Saturday night)

steps.confusionAlert: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת usually means Friday daytime, but here it means Friday night, the first night of שבת itself. That is why a wound would be a שבת problem.

phrases.english: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יִבְעוֹל,
phrases.english: In either case he may not have relations,
not on Shabbat evening
and not at the conclusion of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יִבְעוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First relations with a virgin bride are forbidden on Friday night and on מוצאי שבת

steps.title: Friday night makes sense, but why Saturday night?
steps.stepSummary: Friday night is understood because of חבורה on שבת, but on מוצאי שבת שבת is over, so why is it forbidden? רבי זירא begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense on Friday night, because of making a wound. But on מוצאי שבת, why not? רבי זירא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the Friday night rule but challenges the מוצאי שבת rule. Then it introduces רבי זירא, whose answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First relations with a virgin cause bleeding, which counts as making a wound (חבורה), and that is forbidden on שבת. On מוצאי שבת, שבת has already ended, so that reason no longer applies. The גמרא needs a different reason, and רבי זירא will give it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (accepting one part before challenging another)
Making a wound that draws blood, forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: It makes sense on Shabbat evening —
because of making a wound.
But at the conclusion of Shabbat, why not?
Rabbi Zeira said:

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת מִשּׁוּם חַבּוּרָה, אֶלָּא בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת, אַמַּאי לָא?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of the rule quoted in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ban on first relations on מוצאי שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only obvious reason, חבורה on שבת, does not apply once שבת is over
